threads.thread_goal: Align on scope and target operating model for centralised management.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Launch of Centralised Residential Property Management Model project.
Over the next 30 days we need to land the central operating model, pilot it, and be ready to scale.
I have shared the draft Centralised Property Management Operating Model in A1, which builds on the gap analysis work planned in T1 and the responsibilities matrix in T2.
Before we go further, we need to confirm scope for the first rollout wave and check that the target model in A1 is workable from an operational point of view.
Can each of you review A1 today and comment on:
- which buildings and property types you think we should include in wave one
- any red flags in the proposed responsibilities split
Once we have that, I will formalise the scope and sign off the operating model.

Thanks for sharing A1.
From an operations angle, I suggest we limit wave one to the mid-size residential blocks where we already have regular inspections and stable occupancy.
Concretely, that would be the three 40-unit apartment buildings on Oak Street and the two 25-unit blocks on Riverside.
They are all standard residential, no mixed commercial, which keeps things simpler for the first run.
For T1, I can start mapping current processes for those five buildings first, then extend to others.
On the responsibilities in A1, the split between central team and on-site staff looks broadly workable, but I want to double-check how complaints and urgent maintenance are routed so we do not slow down response times.

From the site side, Oak Street and Riverside are a good starting point.
We already have most unit details and condition notes there, so T1 and later T5 will be easier.
One concern: in A1, some inspection tasks move to the central team.
For safety checks and quick fixes, it is more practical if I keep doing the first pass on site and only escalate bigger issues.
We should also be clear in T2 who logs issues into the system so we do not duplicate work.

On scope: I agree with focusing on standard residential only for wave one.
I would explicitly exclude the serviced apartments and any units with shared commercial space.
Those have different contract structures and service expectations, and they would complicate T2 and the contract pack later.
Regarding A1, the leasing and contract responsibilities look fine, but I suggest we keep initial contract negotiation and any non-standard clauses with the local team, at least during the pilot.
Centralising template management and approvals is good, but we should not slow down deal closure.

I have gone through A1 quickly.
For T2, I can start drafting the RACI matrix based on the roles described there, but I will need confirmation on a couple of points:
- For tenant onboarding, does the central team send all standard communication, or do we keep some messages from the on-site staff
- For billing queries, should tenants contact the central office first, or the building contact
Once we agree on that, I can reflect it clearly in T2 and also align with the future checklist work in T3.

Good points on scope.
Let me summarise what I am hearing so far:
- Include: Oak Street (3 x 40-unit residential blocks) and Riverside (2 x 25-unit residential blocks)
- Exclude for now: serviced apartments and any mixed-use buildings with commercial units
If no one objects, I would like to lock this as the first rollout wave so we can progress T1 and T2 without rework.
On responsibilities, I am comfortable keeping non-standard contract negotiation local during the pilot, with central oversight on templates and approvals as per A1.
Does anyone see a blocker with that approach

No objection from my side.
Limiting the first wave to those five residential blocks is manageable and gives us a good mix of unit sizes.
For responsibilities, I suggest we clarify in T2 that:
- central team owns the standard onboarding communication and documentation
- on-site staff handle the physical handover, meter readings, and immediate condition checks
That aligns with A1 and keeps things practical on the ground.

I am fine with that scope and with keeping non-standard contracts local for now.
For the responsibilities, I just want to make sure T2 states clearly that urgent safety issues can be acted on immediately on site, with central team informed afterwards.
That way we stay compliant and do not delay any critical repairs.

Agree with the scope as summarised.
On the operating model in A1, I have one refinement for T2:
For leasing and contracts, we can define it as:
- central: owns templates, compliance checks, and final approval for exceptions
- local: handles viewings, negotiates within predefined ranges, and collects required documents
This keeps us fast with tenants while ensuring consistency and regulatory alignment.
I can help review the RACI once the first draft is ready.

Understood.
I will reflect that split in the RACI for T2:
- central team: standard onboarding emails, contract pack, and system entries
- on-site: keys, meters, photos, and first inspection
I will also add a note about urgent safety issues being handled immediately on site, as mentioned by 167424.
I will share a draft RACI later today for comments before we call A1 final.

Given the alignment here, I will record the first rollout wave as:
- Oak Street: three residential blocks (40 units each)
- Riverside: two residential blocks (25 units each)
- Excluding serviced apartments and mixed-use buildings for now
That closes the scope decision for wave one so T1 and T2 can proceed.
Next, I want to be sure everyone is comfortable with the overall operating model in A1.
Are there any remaining concerns that would prevent us from approving A1 as the baseline for the pilot

From my side, A1 is workable as long as we incorporate the clarifications we discussed into T2.
The centralised maintenance planning and reporting structure look good, and I can align T1 and later T6 with that.
We may need to fine-tune some details after the pilot, but as a baseline it is solid.

I am comfortable with A1 as well.
The only thing I would like to see in practice is how the reporting tools will work day to day, but that can be tested during the pilot.
For now, the roles and flows described there are clear enough for me to follow.

No blockers from my side.
With the adjustments we have discussed for leasing and contracts, A1 gives us a consistent framework.
I will just want legal to double-check that the central approval steps do not conflict with any local requirements, but that can be handled when we work on T4 and the contract pack.

I am ok with A1 as the baseline.
Once I share the RACI draft for T2, we can make sure the document and the matrix are fully aligned.
From an admin point of view, the centralised contact points and escalation paths are clear enough to start.

Thanks all.
Based on the feedback, I am formally approving the centralised operating model in A1 as our baseline for the pilot.
Any refinements from T2 or later tasks can be handled as controlled updates, but the structure and role split are now fixed for wave one.
I will note this decision in the project notes and inform senior management.

Great, I will proceed on T1 using the confirmed scope and the approved model in A1.
I will map the current processes for the five pilot buildings first and highlight any gaps where the reality on site does not yet match the new model.
I will share a first draft map in a couple of days for review.

I will finalise the initial RACI for T2 based on the approved A1 and share it in this channel.
Once we have your comments, we can record leadership sign-off and move on to the next work packages.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise tenant lifecycle documents and checklists.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the Tenant Onboarding and Changeover Checklist in A2, aligned with the operating model in A1 and the scope we agreed.
This is part of T3 and will also feed into T9 and the contract work in T4.
The checklist currently covers:
- pre-move checks (unit condition, keys, meters)
- move-in steps (documents, photos, handover)
- move-out steps (inspection, keys, final readings)
- basic communication points for tenants
I would appreciate your comments on missing steps, overlaps with existing routines, and anything that might cause confusion for on-site staff or tenants.

Thanks for sharing A2.
Overall structure looks good and matches the flow in A1.
A few suggestions from the housing side:
- In the pre-move section, add a step to check any open maintenance tickets from A4 or the inventory work in T5, so we do not hand over units with unresolved issues.
- For move-in, we should explicitly capture energy performance information and any safety notices we must give tenants.
- For move-out, I would add a reminder to schedule the inspection early enough to respect notice periods and minimise disputes.
These will also help when we build the tenant FAQ in T9.

Looking at A2 from the on-site angle, the sequence is workable, but I would simplify some steps.
For example, the move-in section has separate lines for checking each room; in practice we do a full walk-through and note all issues at once.
Maybe group those into one checklist item with a space for notes.
Also, please add a clear step for handing over building access instructions and emergency contacts.
That reduces questions later and fits with what we already do informally.

From a contracts and compliance perspective, A2 should tie closely to the templates in A3 and the work in T4.
A few points:
- Move-in should explicitly list all documents to be signed or acknowledged: rental agreement, any addenda, building rules, data privacy notices.
- There should be a check that the signed contract in A3 matches the agreed terms and that all mandatory fields are completed.
- For move-out, we should include a step to confirm notice periods and any penalties, so we stay aligned with rental regulations.
These details will also need to be reflected in the tenant FAQ under T9.

Thanks for pulling A2 together.
From a leadership view, I want the checklist to be simple enough for on-site staff to use consistently, but also robust enough to protect us on compliance and disputes.
Please make sure:
- we capture photos and meter readings clearly, as this links to T5 and the inventory in A4
- the steps align with the service levels we plan to communicate to owners and tenants later
Once we converge on content, I will be looking to formally approve A2 for use in the pilot.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.
I will update A2 to:
- add a pre-move check against open maintenance items from A4 and T5
- include explicit steps for energy performance information and safety notices at move-in
- add a reminder to schedule move-out inspections early enough to respect notice periods
I will also simplify the room-by-room checks as suggested by 167424 and add the emergency contact handover.
I will share an updated version shortly.

On the contract side, I will align A2 with A3 and T4 by:
- listing all documents that must be signed or acknowledged at move-in
- adding a check that the signed agreement matches the approved template and agreed terms
- including a step at move-out to confirm notice periods and any applicable penalties
I will also flag in T9 that these points need to be reflected in the tenant FAQ.
Once I have incorporated all of this, I will ask you to do a quick review for any legal gaps.

One more suggestion for A2: in the move-out section, add a step to check for any outstanding rent or charges and to inform tenants clearly about the timeline for deposit return.
This will reduce complaints and ties into the arrears tracking we will later show in the dashboard.
It also gives us a consistent script for staff when tenants move out.

Agree, and from a contract perspective that step should reference the clauses in A3 about deposit handling and arrears.
We should avoid staff improvising explanations.
Maybe in A2 we can point to a short script or to the FAQ under T9, so everyone uses the same wording.

Understood.
I will add a move-out step in A2 to:
- check outstanding rent or charges
- explain deposit timelines based on the clauses in A3
- refer staff to the standard wording that we will include in the T9 FAQ
I will now consolidate all feedback and share a revised A2 for final confirmation.

I have uploaded the updated version of A2.
Changes include:
- streamlined on-site checks and grouped room inspection
- explicit pre-move maintenance and safety checks
- clear list of documents to sign at move-in, aligned with A3
- move-out steps covering notice periods, arrears, and deposit handling
Could you please confirm if this version is ready to use for the pilot, or if there are any final blockers

I have reviewed the updated A2.
The flow is now much easier to follow on site, and all the practical steps we need are there.
From my side, this version is ready to use in the pilot buildings.

I am also happy with the revised A2.
It covers documentation, keys, meter readings, photos, and the main communication points we discussed.
I suggest we approve this version for the pilot and adjust later if the feedback from tenants or staff shows gaps.

Noted.
With confirmation from operations and on-site, I am approving A2 as the standard tenant onboarding and changeover checklist for the pilot.
Please make sure it is uploaded to the shared repository and communicated to staff in the pilot buildings.
Now we need to close on A3 so that contracts are aligned with the checklist and the FAQ under T9.

On A3, I have prepared updated rental agreement and addenda templates under T4.
They are aligned with current regulations and our company policies, and I have already incorporated initial feedback from legal.
Key changes:
- clearer clauses on inspections and access, matching the schedule we are planning
- explicit wording on deposit handling, arrears, and notice periods
- references to the central contact points defined in A1
I would like a quick review from 48703 and 52814 to ensure the operational details match A2 and the planned FAQ in T9.

I have reviewed A3.
The clauses on inspections and access are consistent with what we plan operationally, and the deposit and arrears wording matches what we want staff to explain at move-out.
From the housing side, I am comfortable using these templates in the pilot, provided legal has no outstanding concerns.

I checked A3 against A2.
The list of documents and the key clauses line up with the steps in the checklist.
I do not see any operational conflicts.
Once legal confirms, I think we can approve A3 for the pilot and then reflect the main points in the T9 FAQ.

Legal has confirmed that A3 is aligned with current housing and safety regulations.
Given the operational sign-off from 48703 and 52814, I am approving A3 for use in the pilot buildings.
Please ensure the templates are added to the contract pack and version-controlled as per T4.
We will monitor any issues during the pilot and adjust if needed.

I will upload the approved A2 and A3 to the shared repository, notify on-site staff in the pilot buildings, and start drafting the tenant-facing FAQ and notice templates under T9 so that the wording is consistent.
I will share a first FAQ draft later this week.

threads.thread_goal: Plan maintenance, inspections and compliance activities.

messages.text:
I have drafted an initial proposal for the maintenance and inspection schedule in A5, based on the inventory data we are compiling in A4 under T5 and the operating model in A1.
This is part of T6.
For now, I have grouped buildings into three categories by type and age and suggested inspection frequencies and scope for each.
I would like your input on:
- whether the proposed frequencies are realistic and compliant
- if the scope of each inspection is clear enough for on-site staff
- how we should handle urgent issues versus planned preventive tasks
Once we agree, we can finalise A5 and align it with the compliance checklist in T12.

Looking at A5, the monthly visual checks and annual full inspections for the newer buildings are fine.
For the older Riverside block, I would suggest we keep quarterly checks for common areas, as we already see more wear there.
On scope, it would help if A5 links directly to the compliance checklist from T12, so I know exactly what to look at for fire safety, access, ventilation, and energy items.
That way I can use one list on site instead of switching between documents.

From a regulatory and risk angle, the frequencies in A5 need to align with the minimum requirements for fire safety and energy performance.
For example, some fire equipment checks must be done more often than the general building inspection.
I recommend we:
- use T12 as the baseline for mandatory items and mark them clearly in A5
- distinguish between statutory checks and our own preventive checks
This will also help when we explain the schedule to owners and tenants later.

Thanks for the draft.
I want to make sure the schedule in A5 is both compliant and manageable for on-site staff.
We should avoid overloading 167424 with reporting that does not add value.
Please check that:
- the inspection scope is clearly defined and linked to T12
- urgent issues have a clear escalation path, consistent with the incident procedure we will define later
Once we have a stable proposal, I will sign off on the inspection frequencies and scope for each building category.

Good point on Riverside.
I will adjust A5 so that older blocks have quarterly common-area checks, while newer ones keep the monthly visual and annual full inspections.
I will also link each inspection type in A5 to the relevant sections of the T12 checklist, so you can use one combined list on site.
For urgent issues, I suggest we treat them outside the regular schedule and route them through the incident procedure we will document in A8 and T11.

That works for me.
If A5 clearly marks which checks are statutory from T12 and which are extra, I can plan my time better.
For urgent issues, as long as the incident procedure in A8 allows me to act immediately on safety risks and then log them, we will be fine.

When you update A5, please also:
- mark the items in the schedule that are directly tied to legal requirements from T12
- add a note where external certified contractors are needed, for example for certain fire systems or energy inspections
This will help avoid any confusion about who is allowed to perform which checks.

Understood.
I will revise A5 to:
- differentiate statutory checks from additional preventive ones
- flag items that require external certified contractors
- link each inspection type to the relevant T12 checklist items
Once done, I will share the updated schedule for final review.

From an admin perspective, it would help if A5 also indicates how inspection results feed into A4 and later into the dashboard.
For example, a simple status field for each unit or building that we can update after each inspection.
That will make it easier to track open issues and inspection status without extra spreadsheets.

Good idea.
I will add a status field and a simple coding in A5 that can be mirrored in A4 and later in the dashboard template.
That way we can see at a glance which buildings are up to date on inspections and where there are outstanding issues.

I have now updated A5 with:
- adjusted frequencies for older versus newer buildings
- clear links to T12 items and flags for statutory checks
- notes on when external contractors are required
- a status field that ties into A4
Please review this version and confirm if the inspection frequencies and scope per building category are acceptable.

I have checked the updated A5.
The frequencies and scope look realistic, and the links to T12 make it clear what I need to check.
From the on-site side, I am comfortable working with this schedule.

I have reviewed the revised A5 against the regulatory checklist in T12.
The statutory items are correctly marked, and the proposed frequencies meet or exceed the minimum requirements.
I do not see any compliance gaps.
I recommend we approve this schedule for the pilot.

Thanks for the thorough review.
Based on the feedback, I am confirming the inspection frequency and scope per building category as defined in A5, and we will treat the T12 checklist items as mandatory for all buildings in the portfolio.
This will be our standard for the pilot and for future rollout, unless regulations change.
Please proceed with testing the checklist on at least one building as required by T12.

I will coordinate with 167424 to apply the T12 checklist and the A5 schedule on one of the Oak Street buildings this week.
We will capture any practical issues and adjust wording if needed before full rollout.

Confirmed.
I will run through the T12 checklist on Oak Street Block A and log the results in A4, following the schedule in A5.
I will share feedback on how long it takes and any unclear items.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on KPIs, dashboard structure and reporting cadence.

messages.text:
I have created a first version of the Property Performance Dashboard Template in A6 as part of T7.
It is a simple sheet for now, focused on the pilot buildings.
Current metrics include:
- occupancy rate
- rent arrears
- number of open maintenance issues
- inspection status based on A5
- average resolution time for incidents
I would like your input on which KPIs we should keep, add, or remove, and how often we should update and share this with owners and senior management.

From an operations view, the metrics you listed in A6 are a good start.
I would add:
- number of tenant complaints and their status
- percentage of units with up-to-date inventory and condition data from A4
These will help us see if the centralised model is improving tenant satisfaction and data quality.
For update frequency, I suggest we track most metrics monthly, but keep an internal weekly view on open issues and arrears during the pilot.

I agree with the core KPIs in A6 and the additions suggested by 48703.
I would also consider:
- average time from application to move-in, to see if the new processes speed up leasing
- percentage of contracts using the new A3 templates
These link directly to T4 and the tenant lifecycle work.
For owners, we should keep the view simple: occupancy, arrears, major incidents, and inspection compliance.
More detailed metrics can stay internal.

From the site side, it would help if the KPIs in A6 are easy to update.
If we keep it to a few fields I can update after inspections or incidents, that is fine.
Too many detailed metrics might be hard to maintain.
Maybe we can automate some of the data from A4 and A5 later.

For leadership and owners, I want the dashboard in A6 to answer three questions:
- Are we full enough and collecting rent on time
- Are we keeping buildings safe and in good condition
- Are tenants satisfied and issues resolved quickly
The metrics proposed so far cover most of this.
I would like us to agree on a final list of KPIs and then decide how often we share the summary with owners and senior management.
My initial thought is monthly for owners and monthly or quarterly for senior management, with ad-hoc updates if something material changes.

I will update A6 to include:
- tenant complaints count and status
- percentage of units with up-to-date inventory data from A4
- average time from application to move-in
- percentage of contracts using A3 templates
I will keep the owner-facing view limited to occupancy, arrears, major incidents, and inspection compliance, as suggested.
We can keep the more detailed metrics on a separate internal tab.

On cadence, I support monthly reporting to owners, with a simple one-page summary from A6.
For senior management, a monthly view during the pilot makes sense so we can react quickly if something is off.
After the pilot, we can move to quarterly if things are stable.

I agree with that cadence.
Monthly updates to owners will also help manage expectations around inspections and any planned works.
We should align the reporting dates with the communication plan under T8 so that messages are consistent and not too frequent.

I have updated A6 with the new KPIs and separated the internal and owner views.
Could you please check if the structure is clear and if any metric should still be removed or renamed before we lock it for the pilot

I have reviewed the updated A6.
The metrics are clear and map well to our processes.
I do not see any that we should remove at this stage.
We can always simplify later if we find that some are not useful.

The structure in A6 looks good.
I would just suggest we define clear data owners for each metric in T7, so we know who is responsible for updating what.
For example, arrears from finance, inspections from 167424, and complaints from the central team.

Good point.
I will update T7 to include a simple responsibility table for each KPI in A6, indicating who updates it and how often.
This will also help when we brief finance and other teams.

Based on the latest version of A6 and your feedback, I propose we lock the KPI set as follows for the pilot:
- occupancy rate
- rent arrears
- open maintenance issues and average resolution time
- inspection status and compliance
- tenant complaints and their status
- percentage of units with up-to-date inventory data
- average time from application to move-in
- percentage of contracts using the new templates
For reporting cadence, we will:
- update the dashboard internally on a monthly basis, with weekly internal checks on open issues and arrears during the pilot
- share a monthly summary with owners
- share a monthly summary with senior management during the pilot, then review whether to move to quarterly.
If there are no objections, I will record this as our agreed KPI set and reporting cadence.

No objections from me.
The KPI list and cadence you summarised match what we need to monitor the pilot.
I will make sure our operational data feeds into A6 on time.

I will finalise A6 with the agreed KPIs and set up the monthly reporting schedule in line with T8 so that owner and senior management updates are consistent.
I will also prepare a short guide for data owners on how to update their fields.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare pilot rollout, communication and incident handling approach.

messages.text:
Following our earlier decisions, I propose we use Oak Street Block A and Riverside Block 1 as the two pilot buildings under T10.
Both have a mix of long-term and new tenants and are representative of the wider portfolio.
I have drafted a simple communication outline for tenants and owners, aligned with A7 and the KPIs in A6.
We also need to align this with the incident and escalation procedure in A8 and T11 so that everyone knows how issues will be handled during the pilot.
Feedback welcome on the pilot building choice, start date, and any key messages we should include.

From the site side, Oak Street Block A and Riverside Block 1 are good choices.
I know the tenants there well, and we already have most of the inventory data in A4.
For the start date, I would avoid the first week of next month because we have several planned move-ins.
Mid-month would give us more time to explain the changes and avoid confusion.

I support those two buildings for the pilot.
They are standard residential and the owners have been open to process changes in the past.
For communication, A7 should clearly explain:
- what is changing and what stays the same
- how inspections and maintenance will be scheduled (linking to A5)
- who tenants and owners should contact for different issues, aligned with A8 and T11
We should also reassure owners that they will receive regular reports based on A6.

I can help structure the owner and tenant communication pack in A7, building on the outline you drafted.
We should align the send-out dates with the reporting cadence we agreed in A6 and the broader plan under T8.
For the pilot start date, mid-month as suggested by 167424 works for me, as it gives time to send notices and FAQs under T9.

I am comfortable with Oak Street Block A and Riverside Block 1 as pilot buildings, assuming the owners confirm.
On timing, mid-month next month sounds reasonable.
For communication, I want A7 to be very clear on service levels, escalation paths, and what success looks like for the pilot.
We also need a robust incident and escalation procedure in A8 so that any issues during the pilot are handled consistently and transparently.

On A8 and T11, I have drafted an incident and escalation procedure that:
- defines incident categories and severity levels
- sets response time targets for each severity
- outlines escalation paths from on-site to central team and, if needed, to senior management
It also clarifies when external services (fire brigade, emergency repairs) must be called immediately.
I would like 167424 and 48703 to review it from a practical standpoint before we finalise it for the pilot.

I have looked at A8.
The categories and response times make sense.
One suggestion: for low-severity issues like minor cosmetic defects, we should group them and handle them during the next scheduled visit from A5, instead of treating each as a separate incident.
For high-severity safety issues, it is good that the procedure allows immediate action and then logging afterwards.

I agree with 167424.
A8 should make it clear that minor issues can be batched and addressed during planned maintenance, while anything that affects safety or habitability is treated as urgent.
We should also ensure the escalation paths in A8 match the responsibilities in A1 and the contact points we list in A7.

I will update A8 to:
- clarify that low-severity issues can be grouped and handled during scheduled visits
- emphasise immediate action for safety-related incidents
- align escalation paths with the roles defined in A1 and the contacts in A7
Once updated, I will share it for final confirmation so we can use it in the pilot.

On the communication pack in A7, I will draft:
- an owner letter explaining the centralised model, service levels, and reporting cadence from A6
- a tenant notice explaining what will change in day-to-day interactions and inspections
- a short FAQ aligned with T9 and the incident procedure in A8
I will also propose send-out dates that give tenants at least the required notice before any new inspections.

Given the feedback, I suggest we set the pilot start date for the 15th of next month.
That avoids the busy first week and gives us time to send owner and tenant communications from A7 and the T9 FAQ.
We will need owner confirmation for both buildings before we lock this date.

I have spoken informally with the owners of Oak Street Block A and Riverside Block 1, and they are open to participating in the pilot, subject to seeing the final communication pack.
Assuming no surprises in A7, I am comfortable confirming these two buildings and the 15th of next month as the pilot start date.
We will formalise this once the owner letters are ready.

I have now updated A8 with the agreed changes.
It clearly defines categories, response times, escalation paths, and when to batch minor issues.
Unless there are objections, I suggest we approve A8 as the standard incident and escalation procedure for the pilot.

I have reviewed the updated A8.
The steps are clear and match how we handle issues on site, with better structure.
I am comfortable using this procedure during the pilot.

Same here.
A8 aligns with the operating model and gives clear guidance on when to escalate.
I do not see any gaps from the housing side.

I have uploaded a draft of the owner and tenant communication pack in A7.
It includes the letters, notices, and a short FAQ.
Please review and confirm if this is ready to send once we finalise the pilot date and incident procedure.

I have reviewed A7 and the updated A8.
The communication pack clearly explains the new model, service levels, reporting cadence, and incident handling.
Combined with the confirmed pilot buildings and start date, I am approving A7 and A8 for use in the pilot.
We will monitor feedback closely and adjust if needed before wider rollout.

Great.
I will coordinate with 167424 to brief on-site staff in the two pilot buildings, ensure they understand A7 and A8, and confirm that we are ready to start on the 15th.
We will also set up a simple way to capture tenant and staff feedback during the pilot as required by T10.
